title: Employer Allowance Granted to an Employee Meal Account
content:
Employer allowance is granted on the basis printed against the plan: a daily basis places the allowance on the Employee Meal Account at the start of each service day, a monthly basis on the first day of the calendar month, and a plan whose basis is none is granted nothing at all.

## Lots

Each grant is recorded as its own allowance lot so that spending, lapsing and restoration can be traced lot by lot, and a lot may not exceed the grant ceiling printed against the plan for one grant period. **That last clause is no longer in force**: the ceiling a lot is held to is now the one the current basis for working out a grant establishes, and this document does not restate it.

A lot lapses the number of days printed against the plan after it was granted, and what is left of it is written off unless the plan allows rollover, in which case the unspent balance is carried into the next lot.

## The state the account must stand in

Allowance is only granted while the account stands active or parked for leave, since an enrolled account has no badge in use and a restricted account keeps the allowance it already holds without receiving more. The account's own record settles this before a grant is made, read by the account's reference together with the unspent allowance standing on it.

## Leave, taxable benefit and restoration

Where the plan prorates allowance for leave, a part month of recorded leave reduces the grant in proportion to the working days the employee was actually available; where it does not, the grant is made in full or not at all.

Allowance granted in a year above the taxable benefit ceiling printed against the plan is reported to the employer for payroll treatment, and the grant itself is not reduced.

Allowance restored by a refund is granted back to the lot the spending came from, and where that lot has already lapsed the allowance is not restored at all.

## Basis Q&A

**Does a restricted account go on receiving allowance?** No. It keeps the allowance it already holds and receives no more, the grantable states being active and parked for leave only.

**What happens to a lot that lapses on a plan that allows rollover?** The unspent balance is carried into the next lot rather than written off.

**Is a grant reduced because the year's allowance has passed the taxable benefit ceiling?** No. The excess is reported to the employer for payroll treatment and the grant is made in full.
